notes: Yamamoto-first discovery pass under the current durable editorial rubric. docs/PRIORITIES.md, docs/EDITORIAL.md, docs/DOMAINS.md, and radar/inbox/README.md were read before grading. ALFIE-oriented search, BODY&SOUL, Space M&A, Yamamoto schedule traces, and current Japanese jazz sources produced no new unrecorded Tsuyoshi Yamamoto performance; the currently surfaced Yamamoto dates are already represented in the RADAR. This catch-up restores two Blue Note Tokyo engagements that clear RADAR admission but do not require scarcity inflation: Anoushka Shankar's first Blue Note Tokyo appearance with a sitar-led Chapters quartet, and Christian McBride's Japanese debut of the new Ursa Major ensemble. Both are deliberately A+: strong enough to make room for, but each is part of a broader touring/project context with multiple Tokyo sets rather than a singular one-off.

events.subtitle: Chapters Tour
events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents Anoushka Shankar on October 9-11, 2026. The October 9 sets begin at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM; the October 10-11 sets begin at 4:30 PM and 7:30 PM. The announced quartet is Shankar on sitar, Sarathy Korwar on drums, Tom Farmer on bass, and Arun Ghosh on clarinet. Blue Note identifies the engagement as Shankar's first appearance at the club, while Shankar's official tour calendar lists the three Tokyo dates as part of the Chapters Tour. General web reservations opened May 16, 2026.

en.why_it_matters: This earns a place because the sitar is not being dropped into a generic crossover setting. Shankar brings a compact quartet with Sarathy Korwar, Tom Farmer and Arun Ghosh, giving the instrument room to move between raga-derived phrasing, rhythmic dialogue and contemporary ensemble color. Her first Blue Note Tokyo appearance also puts a musician usually heard in concert halls and festivals into a club scale where attack, resonance and the conversation with drums, bass and clarinet should register very differently.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the six sets if an October Tokyo itinerary intersects these dates, especially if the trip is following instrumental identity and cross-cultural improvisation. The three-night run gives enough flexibility to fit it around scarcer one-offs rather than rebuilding the itinerary around a single performance.

es.why_it_matters: Entra porque el sitar no está metido como adorno dentro de un crossover genérico. Shankar llega con un cuarteto compacto junto a Sarathy Korwar, Tom Farmer y Arun Ghosh, dejando espacio para que el instrumento pase del fraseo de raíz raga al diálogo rítmico y al color de un ensamble contemporáneo. Además es su primera aparición en Blue Note Tokyo: una música que suele escucharse en salas grandes y festivales entra aquí a escala de club, donde el ataque, la resonancia y la conversación con batería, bajo y clarinete deberían sentirse de otra manera.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los seis sets si un itinerario de octubre en Tokio coincide con estas fechas, sobre todo si el viaje viene siguiendo identidad instrumental e improvisación entre tradiciones. Las tres noches dan suficiente flexibilidad para acomodarlo alrededor de encuentros más escasos sin rehacer todo el itinerario por una sola función.

en.why_it_matters: The point is not simply that McBride is one of the defining bassists of his generation. Ursa Major is a new working band built to put younger voices next to his enormous rhythmic and harmonic authority: Nicole Glover's saxophone, Ely Perlman's guitar, Mike King's piano and Savannah Harris's drums give the project a different balance from Inside Straight or New Jawn. Hearing the ensemble make its Japanese debut in a club keeps the emphasis on interaction, bass architecture and what McBride is choosing to build next rather than on repertory from an established band.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the six sets if September in Tokyo lines up, particularly if bass, groove and the next generation of contemporary jazz are central to the trip. Three nights provide enough choice that it should sit comfortably beside rarer one-night events rather than displacing them.
en.listen_before: Christian McBride & Ursa Major — More Is

es.why_it_matters: El punto no es simplemente que McBride sea uno de los bajistas definitorios de su generación. Ursa Major es una banda de trabajo nueva diseñada para poner voces más jóvenes junto a su enorme autoridad rítmica y armónica: el sax de Nicole Glover, la guitarra de Ely Perlman, el piano de Mike King y la batería de Savannah Harris cambian por completo el balance frente a Inside Straight o New Jawn. Escuchar el debut japonés del grupo en un club pone el foco en la interacción, la arquitectura del bajo y en lo que McBride está construyendo ahora, no en repertorio heredado de una banda ya establecida.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los seis sets si septiembre en Tokio coincide, especialmente si bajo, groove y la siguiente generación del jazz contemporáneo forman parte central del viaje. Las tres noches dan margen suficiente para acomodarlo junto a eventos de una sola fecha más raros, sin desplazar éstos.
